articles.body:
Avatar: Seven Havens is an animated cartoon from the creators of the original Avatar: The Last Airbender series. The new series follows twin Avatars as they seek to uncover the past and protect the Seven Havens. The story acts as a follow up to ATLA and The Legend of Korra and takes places about 225 years after the events of the previous series in a world that has experienced technological regression .

Avatar: Seven Havens is a Paramount+ Original series, which means it's currently only available to watch via a Paramount+ subscription . The streaming service has made the move away from airing on Nickelodeon, exclusively the recent Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender movie exclusively on its service as well.

If you're hoping to skip the subscription, Paramount has revealed preorders for a Blu-ray release of season 1 . No release date has been announced just yet.

Avatar: Seven Havens - Season 1 (Blu-ray)

Avatar: Seven Havens will be releasing episodes in batches , with the finale wrapping up on October 30, 2026. There are a total of 13 episodes in season 1 and the series has already been renewed up to season 4 .

Seven Havens is set pretty far in the future and new details are still being revealed with new episodes. As of right now, the main connections to previous Avatar TV shows are rooted in Korra's time as the Avatar. Korra is referenced as the reason for some sort of apocalyptic event that destroyed the world, which is referenced in the opening credits and as a festival play in the first episode. It's unclear exactly what exactly Korra did, but the event is likely tied to her choosing to keep the spirit portals open, rather than keeping the worlds separate.

The other obvious lore connection in the new series is the existence of The White Lotus. Karthik talks a bit about the order to Jae in the early episodes and we get a look at a picture of Iroh in the background. Not much else is said about the order other than that it still exists in dwindling numbers.

Finally, we get a bit of a hint in episode 3 that the long-running "my cabbages!" joke is likely going to make a comeback . This is referenced when a cart full of what appears to be cauliflower nearly gets destroyed by an out-of-control Camel-Amadillo. This small detail proves that cabbages do likely exist in this post-apocalyptic world.

articles.title: Ceres Research Station - Super Metroid Guide - IGN
articles.summary: The last Metroid is in captivity, the galaxy is at
articles.body:
The last Metroid is in captivity, the galaxy is at peace.

"I first battled the Metroids on Planet Zebes. It was there that I foiled the plans of the Space Pirate Leader Mother Brain to use the creatures to attack Galactic Civilization.

I next fought the Metroids on their homeworld, SR388. I completely eradicated them except for a larva, which after hatching followed me like a confused child... I personally delivered it to the Galactic Research Station at Ceres so scientists could study its energy producing qualities.

The scientists' findings were astounding! They discovered that the powers of the Metroid might be harnessed for the good of civilization!

Satisfied that all was well, I left the station to seek a new bounty to hunt. But, I had hardly gone beyond the asteroid belt when I picked up a distress signal.

Samus Aran's adventure in Super Metroid starts with a prologue sequence on Ceres Research Station. This is a self-enclosed area that introduces the setting and controls, but doesn't involve exploration or puzzle solving.

After her narrated intro about the attack on the station, you will begin with Samus standing on an elevator. Use the D-pad (or Left Stick , if you're playing on a modern controller) to drop down and jump from platform to platform until you reach the bottom.

Approach or shoot the unlocked hatch to your right, enter, and continue to the right until you reach the hatch that leads to the next room. You can run faster by holding B .

In this room follow the stairs downwards for two flights until you reach a door to your right.

Enter and continue to the right. Something has happened as all the scientists are dead.

Pass through a long hallway until you reach a small room with a Metroid -- in a jar -- sitting on the floor.

As you approach the Metroid, Ridley will appear in the background. This is your first Boss battle.

The only weapon you have in this section is the basic beam, which you fire with X . Though presented as a boss battle, this is really just a peek at the big bad arch nemesis. You can't win here.

Shoot Ridley as often as you like -- there is no point in dodging its attacks, as once your energy is below 30 Ridley will dive bomb you and then flee the room.

After Ridley has fled, a countdown begins and you only have 60 seconds to escape the Space Colony.

Exit through the door you came through, to your left, and follow the route back to the elevator at the beginning of this section. Steam from burst vents and falling tiles do no damage, but they do slow you down so try and avoid them.

As you ascend in the shaft by jumping with A , the entire station will start to tilt. Note that you have two different jumps, a flip (push left or right and jump) and a standard jump up (don't push left or right to jump).

The latter is a faster option for this area. Not that you'll run out of time as one minute is a big window to escape the station.

Can You Fail the Prologue Escape Sequence?

Yes! If you take too long and the timer runs out, a cutscene will show the station blowing up and you'll be presented with a Game Over screen. You can restart the mission or exit to the title.

Once you reach the elevator, a cut scene will start, Ceres Station will blow up, and Samus will escape the Space Station.

She will head to the nearby Planet Zebes.

articles.title: Tested: Nvidia’s GeForce Now just breathed new life into my Steam Deck
articles.summary: The Verge tests Nvidia’s cloud gaming service GeForce Now on the Steam Deck, now that it has a native app.
articles.body: I don’t want gaming to become another streaming subscription service that keeps going up in price. I don’t want to put even more power in Nvidia’s hands, particularly not right now. But I can’t deny that the company’s $20-a-month* GeForce Now is a near-perfect fit for the Steam Deck. I’ve been covering cloud gaming for 15 years, and this is the very first time I’ve wanted to keep playing indefinitely. --- What is GeForce Now? For the uninitiated, Nvidia’s GeForce Now is a game streaming service that farms the graphical processing power out to the cloud. Instead of controlling a game running locally on your Steam Deck’s chip, you’re effectively remote-controlling an RTX 4080-powered* gaming rig in a server farm many miles away, which you sync with your existing Steam, Epic, Ubisoft, Xbox, and Battle.net accounts to access your games and savegames from the cloud. *Nvidia’s GeForce Now also technically has a free tier, and a “Performance” tier, but I recommend you ignore both. For me, it was the difference between playing many games through a clean window or a dirty window, the difference between playing Alan Wake II and Indiana Jones with full ray tracing or none at all, the difference between comfortably stretching to 4K or not. --- Handhelds have already become my favorite way to play games. The Steam Deck is comfortable and easy to pick up whenever and wherever the mood strikes. But neither my Deck nor my aging desktop PC have kept up with the latest titles. Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 and Baldur’s Gate 3 can look like a fuzzy mess on a Deck, and I’ve never seen Alan Wake II, Portal RTX and Indiana Jones and the Great Circle in all their ray-traced glory on my RTX 3060 Ti desktop. But today, with Nvidia’s just-now-released GeForce Now app for the Steam Deck, I can play every one of those titles at near-max settings, anywhere in my home, for hours and hours on a charge. And if I dock that Steam Deck to my 4K TV, it can output 4K60 HDR and/or ray-traced graphics that put the PS5 Pro to shame. When we tested GeForce Now’s last big upgrade in 2023, Tom and I agreed it wasn’t quite on par with playing on a native PC. But on a Steam Deck, where I’m either playing on a low-res handheld screen or sitting across the room from a TV where I don’t notice so many imperfections, it can feel like the best of both worlds. Here’s what Expedition 33 looks like running natively on my Steam Deck today, versus the Deck with GeForce Now: [Image: Running natively on Steam Deck leaves something to be desired. Tap for full-size image. [Image: Running on GeForce Now, I could play at 1920 x 1200 with Epic spec and no DLSS required. Tap for full-size image. The best part might be this: while handhelds like the Steam Deck barely get two hours of such a game at potato graphical settings, I could get 7 to 8 hours of GeForce Now. I saw the cloud gaming service consistently sip under 7 watts from my Steam Deck OLED’s 49.2 watt-hour battery, barely more than the system consumes at idle. And the new native app makes it a cinch to set up, with no more web browser-and-script workaround: just hold down the power button and switch to desktop mode, download the app, run it, and scan QR codes with your phone to link your various accounts. Oh, you’d best believe there are caveats. Giant gaping gotchas galore, which I’ll explain as we go. But after testing the service for nearly two weeks, I’m starting to believe in cloud gaming again. Now, you might be wondering: how the heck am I playing a game where timing is so critical via remote control? Here’s the first big caveat: you need a low-latency internet connection, a good Wi-Fi router or wired ethernet, and you need to be within range of Nvidia’s servers for the magic to work. Download speed isn’t as key: 50Mbps should suffice for 4K, and you can get away with less. But I’m armed with a AT&T Fiber connection, and I live maybe 30 minutes away from Nvidia’s San Jose, California servers, which makes me a best-case scenario for this tech. Still, Nvidia has over 35 worldwide data centers now, including 14 distinct locations in the United States, and my colleagues with Xfinity and Spectrum cable internet in Portland and Brooklyn tell me Expedition 33 played just as well for them. [Image: Rough server locations for GeForce Now; you can get a better idea by “The latency was negligible to the point that I wasn’t missing parries,” Cameron Faulkner tells me, saying he nailed the Sad Troubadour on the first try. Jay Peters and I found we needed to adjust our timing a bit, but I wound up playing roughly half the game over GeForce Now and almost never looked back. Even with the best of connections, though, GeForce Now isn’t bulletproof. Once or twice a day, my seemingly stable gameplay session would at least briefly unravel into a choppy mess. In single-player games like Expedition 33 and Indiana Jones I could easily forgive a few minutes of trouble, but my colleagues Antonio Di Benedetto and Erick Gomez saw it in otherwise stable twitch shooters where lag could be a bigger issue. “I saw a handful of lag spikes / hiccups that would definitely screw anybody over in a competitive shooter, but thankfully they weren’t at the worst times and they soon subsided,” Antonio tells me. You also give up some of the Steam Deck’s portability. While you can plug and unplug the Steam Deck from a TV dock and seamlessly switch between big screen and small screen play, you can’t just put the Steam Deck to sleep without ending the session and losing unsaved progress. (Unlike, say, Chiaki.) And although the native GeForce Now app supports 4K60, a big leap up from 1440p, you may find yourself squinting at tiny text because it doesn’t scale the UI appropriately. Also: while GeForce Now also supports a lower res but smoother 1440p 120Hz mode on TVs and even other gaming handhelds, it doesn’t offer a 90Hz mode for the Deck OLED yet. I tested at 60Hz instead. [Image: Tiny text. Speaking of portability, public Wi-Fi generally isn’t good enough for GeForce Now, and neither are most cellular connections — even with four bars of Verizon 5G UWB service and a wired USB tether to my phone, my stream quickly deteriorated into the jumble you see below. Only the very best cellular connection in my entire neighborhood, a spot right under a 5G tower where I can get 1,200Mbps down and 30 millisecond ping, felt playable to me. [Image: This is on four bars of Verizon 5G UW. It actually got worse after this, with ping in the 500ms range. And, as we’ve discussed previously, only the $20-a-month Ultimate tier truly shows what cloud gaming is capable of. Expedition 33 looked substantially worse on the Performance tier (Epic spec, native resolution, vs. Medium spec, 50 percent resolution with DLSS) and Indiana Jones went from gorgeous to just “playable while handheld” for me. But the biggest caveat with GeForce Now may be outside the company’s control: you have to bring your own games, and yet you only can bring games where Nvidia has explicitly struck a distribution deal. Nvidia has made progress: 165 of my 457 Steam games are now available to play, up from 85 two years ago. The company offers over 2,100 games in total across Epic, Battle.net, Ubisoft, Xbox, and GOG too. But Nvidia has no games from Sony, so I’m not playing Helldivers 2, no games from Rockstar, so I’m not playing GTA V or Red Dead Redemption 2, and no Elden Ring, no PUBG, no Schedule I or Football Manager or FIFA or NBA or The Sims. We never quite know which games GeForce Now will get, or when, or if they might disappear. Cloud gaming has never felt like a better deal, now that the service has matured, now that handhelds can make such good use of it, and now that buying your own GPU is such a ridiculously expensive proposition. Maybe I’ll defer my own next GPU upgrade in favor of a subscription. But it’s not for everyone — you should definitely try a $8 GeForce Now Ultimate day pass first — and there’s still a lot of mental friction. I’m not looking forward to the day that Nvidia alters the deal further.

articles.title: Former Xbox studios Double Fine and Compulsion will keep games after going indie
articles.summary: Double Fine and Compulsion Games will become “independent studios with their IP, catalog, and runway for their next games,” says Xbox CEO Asha Sharma.
articles.body: Microsoft is spinning off four of its Xbox game studios — Compulsion Games, Double Fine Productions, Ninja Theory, and Undead Labs — as part of the restructuring announced today. However, two that are going independent, Double Fine and Compulsion, will get to keep their franchises and games catalogs, according to Xbox CEO Asha Sharma. “Compulsion Games and Double Fine Productions will return to management and transition to independent studios with their IP, catalog, and runway for their next games,” Sharma says in a memo. Compulsion and Double Fine have also shared statements about their futures. Here’s Compulsion’s: > When Compulsion Games was founded in 2009 as an independent studio, we were just a few dreamers in a leaky old gramophone factory devoted to creating rich storylines and experiences that felt handcrafted. We care about the craft of making games, the stories we tell, the players who experience them, and the assembled creators who put their heart and soul into doing something different. > Today, we’re sharing that Compulsion Games will return to independent management following our time as part of XBOX. As part of this transition, we will retain the rights to Contrast, We Happy Few, and our award-winning South of Midnight. We’re grateful for the years we spent with XBOX, for the support they provided our team, and for the opportunity to bring these games to players around the world. As an independent studio, we’re excited to continue building the distinctive games that define Compulsion while taking the next steps in our journey. > Our immediate priority is to support our team throughout this transition period. We are confident in the future of Compulsion Games and look forward to this next chapter where one thing will remain constant: we will create unique games that tell important stories, all with the goal of touching the hearts and minds of our players. And here’s what Double Fine, the studio behind games like Psychonauts, Keeper, and Kiln, had to say: > Once again, Double Fine Productions will be an independent studio. > We’re thankful to everyone at Xbox for seven great years together, and for working with us to reach an outcome which preserves our history and culture, and returns ownership of our games to us. > To everyone who has reached out to us these past few weeks: Thank you so much for all your kind words, we’ve been deeply touched by all your messages. We will share more news soon on what comes next. > Your continued support is greatly appreciated, > Tim & All at Double Fine As for the other two studios, Ninja Theory and Undead Labs, they have “entered terms to join new ownership with funding to complete and grow” their next announced games, Senua and State of Decay 3, Sharma says. Meanwhile, when it comes to Arkane Studios, which is working on a Blade game, “management is beginning required consultation with its Works Council to review potential strategic options.”

articles.title: 4K Blu-ray Releases - Avatar: Seven Havens Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Avatar: Seven Havens has wrapped up episodes for season 1. and Paramount has already revealed Blu-ray preorders at Amazon. Without any sort of release date
articles.body:
Avatar: Seven Havens has wrapped up episodes for season 1 . and Paramount has already revealed Blu-ray preorders at Amazon . Without any sort of release date attached at the moment, the only way to watch these new episodes is via a Paramount+ subscription.

That being said, we now know that the physical home release will actually be happening. Both Avatar: The Last Airbender and The Legend of Korra were released as as individual seasons and as a box set at the end of their run. While the new show is a Paramount+ original series and that could affect release timing, the most recent Avatar Aang movie is what we can likely base our expectations on.

When to Expect an Avatar: Seven Havens Blu-ray Release

Avatar: Seven Havens wraped up its first season on October 30 with the last batch of episodes. So at the very least you shouldn't expect any sort of announcement about a home release date until further into November. If we look at the timeline for the Avatar Aang movie Blu-ray , it's unlikely we'll see any sort of date go live until more than a month after the series wraps up. And if that movie is any indication of when the home release will actually arrive at your door, you're likely looking at another six month wait once preorders go live.

So following that logic, the earliest you could expect preorders for Avatar: Seven Havens on Blu-ray would be sometime in early December, followed by a June 2026 release. Pair that with the fact that many folks are only signing up for a Paramount+ subscription to watch the new Avatar show and it's a pretty long wait.

articles.title: Self-Made Millionaire Says Buying GTA 6 Saves You $5,000
articles.summary: British self-made millionaire, entrepreneur, and social media educator Mark Tilbury put out a video giving the most sound financial advice of 2026: buy GTA 6. According to him, it’ll save you a big chunk of change.
articles.body:
British self-made millionaire, entrepreneur, and social media educator Mark Tilbury put out a video giving the most sound financial advice of 2026: buy GTA 6 . According to him, it’ll save you a big chunk of change.

“GTA 6 costs $99.99,” he said, going straight for the more expensive Ultimate Edition rather than the $80 standard edition (perhaps he, like many others, consider the Ultimate Edition and its extra contents to be the default version). “If it takes you 80 hours to complete, that’s $1.25 per hour of fun. But once you add in side missions and explore the map, it’s down to 50 cents an hour.

“Now let’s say you play for four hours every evening, that’s 50 nights of entertainment. Compare that to going out, where you could easily spend $100 in a single night. That’s why buying GTA 6 actually saves you $5,000.”

Obviously the video is tongue-in-cheek and not actual financial advice (who’s going out 50 nights in a row and spending $100 a pop?). But it’s actually a fair point on the value proposition of the game. An investment in your time, if you will.

That’s why publishers are reportedly hoping GTA 6 sets a new precedent on game pricing — other companies will struggle to compete with its size and scale. It seems like the kind of game you could play for hundreds of hours, and that’s before GTA Online even comes into the equation.

“I’m a 40yo gamer, don't drink much, don't smoke, don't do drugs or go out with friends,” said one commenter. “This is how I explain me gaming to people.”

In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023

“Straight to mum,” said another. “Rockstar paid a billion dollars for it, so it’s a steal at the end of the day,” said another mathematician.

Tilbury is a businessman best known for his videos on frugal living. Despite being a millionaire, he reuses old cups, flies economy, wears the same rotation of clothes, and avoids luxury hotels.

articles.title: How to Beat Jing Ye, The Outlaw in Phantom Blade Zero - Phantom Blade Zero Guide - IGN
articles.summary: In terms of story boss difficulty in Phantom Blade Zero, it was pretty smooth sailing for me until I ran into Jing Ye, the mounted jackass. Thankfully, once
articles.body:
In terms of story boss difficulty in Phantom Blade Zero, it was pretty smooth sailing for me until I ran into Jing Ye, the mounted jackass. Thankfully, once you know how to deal with his nonsense, he’s considerably easier to take down, even on Hellwalker difficulty, where I made sure to test these same strategies. Here’s your full guide to taking down Jing Ye, The Outlaw , in Phantom Blade Zero.

Before getting into the fight proper, let’s discuss what equipment you should be bringing into this battle, starting with accessories .

There’s certainly a bit of wiggle room here since most everything other than the Preservation Jar (since he doesn’t use poison) can be useful. I went with these three:

Medicine Case , which increases the amount you heal when using Medicine since he hits really hard.

Cavalrybane , which increases the damage you do to mounted enemies by 25%.

And the Shieldbreaker Talisman , since dealing with his spiked shield after knocking him off his stupid horse is a huge priority.

As far as weapons go, make sure the two you have equipped are upgraded as much as you can, and make one of those Jagged Steel , since most of the damage you inflict will be while he’s guard broken, and Jagged Steel’s level 5 ability does a ton of extra bleed buildup.

For the other, I went with Sanguine Twin since Chi-Infused Blade is nice for dealing some extra damage, and I was comfortable with the rhythm of its attacks at this point. But really anything paired with Jagged Steel will work; you just need an alternate weapon to switch to when your Sha-Chi runs low.

For Phantom Edges , the only one I really used was the Dread Axe for breaking his shield after knocking him off his horse. Make sure it’s at least level 5 so you can use the instant full power charge. It costs two remnant sparks, but it’s absolutely worth it. When your loadout is all set, go ahead and approach him.

I’m gonna break this fight down into two phases, one on his horse and one off, but just know that every time you die, the fight starts completely over, unlike some other bosses that let you continue from later phases on retries. It’s probably because you don’t have to take his health bar down all the way to start the second part.

To open this fight, unless you rush in close, he’ll most likely do one of two things– throw out a very fast projectile that you can’t even really see travel (it just looks like he’s gearing up for a slash), or he’ll leap at you. One leap is a blue flash that you can parry, and one is black that you’ll have to dodge. If you’re ready for them, they’re both pretty easy to react to.

For this phase of the fight, the ideal distance you’ll want to keep from him is just out of his sword’s reach. He has some well-telegraphed blue and red flashing melee attacks that you’ll want to be close enough to take advantage of to deal Sha-Chi damage, but he also has a very troublesome ranged attack you’ll want to be able to back away and deal with.

That troublesome attack I spoke of would be his blood knives , and there are three different animations for them.

For the first, the horse will whinny and rear back, and the knives will rush towards you and home in as soon as the horse’s front hooves hit the ground.

For the second one, he’ll toss something into the air, grab it, and crush it in his fist, summoning the knives. He can also keep crushing more to summon more groups of knives, so be on the lookout of more coming right behind.

For the third, he’ll toss a ball up into the air, and hit it with his sword.

Whichever way he summons them, the best way to deal with the knives is to dodge to the side , and I do want to emphasize to the side . This gives you the best chance to dodge all of them if you dodge with the right rhythm. You can keep going in one direction, or back and forth. You can block or even parry some of these knives if you run out of room to dodge, or you’re too close to avoid the knives, but it’s really not ideal. Since it’s hard to see exactly when they’re about to hit, the parry is hard to time. And because it’s not doing Sha-Chi damage to Jing Ye since it’s a projectile, there’s really no benefit as you’ll probably be losing some Sha-Chi yourself. And lastly, even while guarding, you’ll be taking bleed damage and you’ll lose a big chunk of health if the bleed meter fills up all the way. Better to avoid the knives altogether.

Another big reason to dodge is that Jing Ye will often launch one of three attacks while you’re dealing with the knives– either the projectile or his big leap attack, in both the blue and black flash variations. Dodging at a steady pace but not spamming it is the best way to be ready to parry the projectile and blue leap, and also be able to dodge the black leap as well. If Soul starts cartwheeling, you can get caught with one of these attacks mid animation. Better to keep the dodges not too fast and consistent to be ready for whatever he throws at you. The correct rhythm is more important than speed. Make sure to keep your eyes on him while dodging the knives to see what he’s planning.

Other than the knives, there’s only a few more attacks you need to look out for. The first is a three-hit slash that ends with a red attack, meaning you’ll need to dodge. This sequence starts with an underhand swing, and then a cut across his body, so it’s easy to spot. He also has several blue slashes that are easy to react to if you keep enough distance, and the two different leaps with the blue and black flashes.

And the last thing you’ll need to be ready for is when he kicks up dust with his sword. This is another good reason to keep a little bit of distance, as he’s much harder to block or dodge when your vision is obscured, so you’ll need to be ready to back up. The rest of his attacks are just standard swings, and they’re pretty easy to parry. The blood knives are the big thing to look out for.

The last tip for this phase is to just not get greedy; you’ll do plenty of Sha-Chi damage just from parrying his melee blows, and dealing with his red and blue attacks.

Keep in mind that even after a Ghoststep counter, he’ll start swinging pretty immediately if you close the distance. You may get a hit or two in, but be ready to parry his swings immediately. As long as you can deal with his blood knives, take your opportunities to parry his melee attacks and get your ghoststep counters in on red and blue attacks, you’ll guard break him pretty quickly. Once he’s stunned, use Jagged Steel’s Blood Blade ability to try and score some extra bleed buildup, and then use your Sha-Chi essence with L2 or the left trigger if you have it, keep spamming Sha-Chi attacks, and then switch weapons as the guard break ends to refill your meter and prepare for defense.

If you’re making the most of your damage phases, you’ll probably knock him off his horse during the second guard break, and I’ve even done it during the first a few times. Once he’s off his high horse, the second phase begins.

As I mentioned earlier, the immediate need is to take care of his shield. It causes a ton of bleed damage and is just a huge nuisance to deal with. Don’t wait– as soon as you see him get knocked off, unleash a fully charged Dread Axe attack by jamming on R2 or the Right Trigger. This is why we want the Dread Axe to at least be level 5. If that doesn’t break his shield all the way, one more uncharged hit should do it. This will leave him guard-broken as well, which means you get to unleash a full damage phase on him. This should take him down to about half health straight away.

After breaking his shield, you have some similar but slightly different attacks to deal with. The blood knives return, but in a smaller number this time– usually only one group you have to avoid. While that’s nice, he’ll usually pair it with another sequence where he runs to the side to kick dust into the air to obscure himself, before leaping out of it to catch you by surprise.

Even when I knew he was coming, this attack still hit me quite a few times. He leaps at you really fast, so you’ll probably need to dodge earlier than you’re expecting. After the leap attack, he’ll either turn his back to you and follow up with a blue slash (if you miss the parry he’ll throw dirt in your face afterward), or pommel strike you quickly and follow up with a red grab.

Do not get hit by this. He’ll saw into your shoulder for major damage and restore his own health at the same time.

Other than these flashy attacks, he has several segments of combos that he can do all together or in parts. These include a turn around slash followed by either flinging dirt at you, or two quick overhead smashes. A kick followed by a run into a delayed slash. A move where he kicks his sword straight up with an uppercut slash, into a second slash, and then a blue attack. And a move where he kicks his sword to the side, slashes once, and then does a red attack.

He also will sometimes do that black flash leap even when not behind his smokescreen.

That sounds like a lot, but these attacks aren’t hard to avoid if you know what’s coming, and parrying most of it will take his Sha-Chi meter almost all the way down.

As long as you avoid his grab, don’t overspend on your Sha-Chi meter, prepare yourself to dodge his leap out of the dirt cloud, and keep yourself healed up, you’ll break his guard in no time with a few parries. Then you just lay into him again with your most damaging sequence, and if he’s guard-broken with low health, the button prompt for an execution will pop up. Press it, you win the fight, and he’ll fall like all the same before him.

When you beat him, you’ll earn his weapon, the Outlaw Warblade, which has some pretty cool properties. You can spend your own HP and give yourself recoverable damage to unleash powerful attacks, and then heal it with your standard combo. You can also perform the hit-grab he used on you that allows you to recover quite a bit of health.

articles.title: Nintendo Reveals Development Team Behind The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake
articles.summary: Nintendo has revealed the development team responsible for creating The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake.
articles.body:
Nintendo has revealed the development team responsible for creating The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake .

The Super Mario Bros. company typically keeps its cards pretty close to its chest when it comes to the behind-the-scenes details for its biggest releases. The Legend of Zelda series is no exception, but Nintendo did offer a peek behind the curtain as part of an Ocarina of Time remake installment in its Ask the Developer Q&A series.

Fans have speculated who might be behind the Nintendo Switch 2 reimagining of an all-time classic since it was announced. While some believed Xenoblade series developer Monolith Soft might be leading the charge, for example, the interview confirmed that it's actually Nintendo's Entertainment Planning & Development (EDP) Production Group No. 3 that's responsible for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake.

Featured in the first interview chapter are franchise producer Eiji Aonuma and series directing veteran Hidemaro Fujibayashi, with EDP Production Group No. 3's HokWai Ng, Aya Shida, Hiroki Taguchi, and Masato Ohashi also listed as interviewees to be featured in future highlights. In other words, the core team behind one of the most highly-anticipated games of the last few years is the same group behind most The Legend of Zelda projects from the last 30 years.

Longtime fans of the original Nintendo 64 game (or even its 2011 Nintendo 3DS remake) who have feared the Switch 2 version of the story could tarnish its reputation can probably rest easy knowing it was in experienced hands. That said, it is always possible another team like Monolith Soft could have chipped in as a support developer, though we likely won't know the full list of team members until we have a better look at those credits in a few days.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake launches for Switch 2 November 5. Although it was made by the same hands that have helped keep the classic fantasy franchise kicking for decades, that doesn't mean the developers weren't willing to experiment where they could. During the interview, Aonuma explained that he tried to "basically let the developers make whatever changes they genuinely felt were necessary."

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Preview Screenshots

"I wanted the team to make The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time their own, and to follow through on their own ideas about what the game should be," he added. "That said, I did deliver my fair share of lectures along the way. (Laughs) I took a step back to observe how the younger members of the development team would reimagine The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time using the insights and answers they had arrived at on their own."

Fujibayashi added that, from his point of view, it was important for the team to have a clear outline for what would and wouldn't be changed from the Nintendo 64 game early on.

"For people like us, who know both the original The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time and the recent 3D Legend of Zelda games, there's no shortage of things we’d like to say when it comes to designing a game," he said. "(Laughs) That’s why I took a step back and supported the team from a broader perspective by helping them clarify the things they needed to be mindful of when designing the game."

Nintendo Switch 2: The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Edition Console Images

Despite having a good plan for how Nintendo and EDP Production Group No. 3 would tackle The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake from the get-go, Aonuma recently admitted that he's still a bit nervous to see how fans will respond . Meanwhile, Google recently launched a time-traveling Easter Egg to help build up hype for this week's new Switch 2 game.

articles.title: Latest Steam Hardware Survey Shows Just How Hard PC Gamers Have Been Hit by AI
articles.summary: The entirety of 2026 has been marked by continually rising hardware prices, and now, according to the latest Steam Hardware Survey, the average gaming PC is starting to embrace older hardware once more.
articles.body:
The entirety of 2026 has been marked by continually rising hardware prices, and now, according to the latest Steam Hardware Survey, the average gaming PC is starting to embrace older hardware once more.

The October Steam Hardware Survey went live yesterday, and it's clear that the state of PC hardware is causing gamers to be a bit more frugal with their builds. The biggest sign of this is in the RAM configuration, where systems using 16GB of RAM have now taken the top spot, rising 3.6% to cover 41.42% of the Steam user base. Users with a 32GB configuration have diminished at the same time, dropping 5.16%, to cover 37.06% of Steam users.

But it's not just RAM that people are cutting back on. For graphics cards, the RTX 3060 has reclaimed its top spot, growing 0.08%, and now representing 3.62% of all Steam users. That doesn't seem like a lot, but considering the huge amount of GPUs that exist, it's a significant proportion. It probably doesn't hurt that you can get an RTX 3060 used on eBay for around $250–300 right now. For CPUs, 8-core CPUs saw a decline in favor of 4-core CPUs, which rose 1.57% to cover 12.36% of PCs with Steam.

It's not hard to see why people are opting for less powerful PCs right now. Pretty much every PC component has gone up in price over the last year, to the point where high-end GPUs are flat-out disappearing from retailer's listings .

Meanwhile, Samsung's latest earnings report suggests that the RAM crisis is only going to get worse next year, as that company gears up to forward even more memory to AI data centers. And while all of this is going on, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman even came out and suggested that it's 'quite terrible' for people to have RAM in their own computers.

It's not just gaming PCs that are getting hit by this ongoing RAM crisis. The PS5 Pro sold out ahead of GTA 6, prompting retailers to charge upwards of $1,399 for used consoles , and Microsoft started asking people to sell unused Xboxes . In the face of all this, it becomes less shocking when rumors appear suggesting that the next-generation Xbox is going to cost $1,800 .

But at least when faced with these higher RAM prices, PC builders have the choice to opt for a lower-end configuration, and that's exactly what's happening with the latest Steam Hardware Survey.

Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

articles.title: Nintendo Explains Why It Chose to Do Another The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake
articles.summary: Nintendo has explained why it chose to develop another The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake.
articles.body:
Nintendo has explained why it chose to develop another The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake .

Franchise producer Eiji Aonuma was asked what sparked the team's desire to return to one of the most treasured stories in gaming history during the first installment in a series of Ask the Developer Q&A posts. It's an in-depth chat about what it was like to revisit a classic game for Nintendo Switch 2, and how it came about in the first place.

The reimagining set to launch in just a few short days will mark the second time Nintendo has remade The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (the first launched for the Nintendo 3DS in 2011 ). Aonuma explained that there were a number of factors Entertainment Planning & Development (EDP) Production Group No. 3 had in mind, with its 40th anniversary being one of the most important.

60 The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Switch 2 Screenshots

"This year marks the 40th anniversary of the very first Legend of Zelda game," Aonuma said. "With that in mind, I was thinking about what I should create as the producer of the series. Many of the team members who work alongside me on Legend of Zelda games today have only experienced developing the more recent titles. That led me to wonder, 'Do they truly understand just how significant The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time was to the series as a whole?'"

Aonuma makes a good point. Although he worked on the original Nintendo 64 game when it launched in 1998 and has carried that experience through subsequent entries in the series in the decades since, there are plenty of team members who don't have that same familiarity with its past.

Sure, there are those with a passing familiarity with the original The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time or those who have at least played it, but Aonuma started to wonder how they'd interpret the game "as they go about developing future Legend of Zelda games." Allowing them to not only revisit that original story but also leave their own stamp on it, he believes, could help bolster whatever new The Legend of Zelda games come next.

"By learning the game structure and development style behind the original The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, and by actually rebuilding it as a full remake," he added, "it may trigger new insights that they can carry forward into future development. If we could achieve that, I thought it would be incredibly valuable. That’s what led us to the conclusion that now is the right time to revisit The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time once again."

Aonuma elaborated, saying that there were many elements considered when choosing to develop a The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2. The team wanted players who had grown used to the open structure of games like Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom to enjoy the fun of "progressing through a carefully paced adventure and story" that is "gradually building up the player’s growth and their understanding of the narrative along the way."

Nintendo's latest The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake launches for Switch 2 November 5. Despite having decades of experience and solid reasoning backing the decision to do a remake, Aonuma recently said he's still "nervous" to see what players think . While we wait to get our hands on the launch build, you can see what IGN thought in our hands-on preview .

articles.title: Gearbox Calls on Fans to Help Shape the Next Borderlands, Teases 'Exciting Overall Direction' For the Future of the Franchise
articles.summary: Borderlands developer Gearbox has called on fans to let it know what they want next from the next game in the franchise, as work begins on “an exciting overall direction.”
articles.body:
Borderlands developer Gearbox has called on fans to let it know what they want next from the next game in the franchise, as work begins on “an exciting overall direction.”

Borderlands 4 just wrapped up its Year 1 of DLC, and in a note to fans today, Gearbox issued its long-awaited future content announcement, confirming more is coming to the looter shooter next year. “Moving forward, Weekly Activity refreshes and Community Challenges will continue,” Gearbox said. “We just wrapped our Year 1 roadmap, and the team is cooking hard on more Borderlands 4 content for next year.” What this content involves beyond Weekly Activity refreshes and Community Challenges was not specified.

Gearbox then spoke vaguely about its plans for the future of the Borderlands franchise, asking fans for their opinions.

“The team is constantly listening to community feedback, and they are exploring additional character arcs, storylines, and an exciting overall direction for the future of the franchise,” Gearbox said.

The studio continued: “... we’re also taking a bigger look at the franchise as a whole. Where can we take it next? What characters do you want to spend more time with? What stories deserve a payoff? A huge part of that is listening to you. Keep the conversation going - we're listening. Tell us what you think! Share your thoughts with us on social and tune into the Gearbox Devcast. We’re always responding to community feedback on that show.”

Don’t hold your breath for the announcement of Borderlands 5 or whatever the next game ends up being called, however. It sounds like early days.

“All that said, big plans take time, and we need some room to work,” Gearbox added. “You can trust that we’ll talk more when the time is right. Now is your chance to influence what we’ll say. We’re listening and we’re working hard for you. Thanks for being with us in the Borderlands.”

The announcement comes as the Borderlands franchise crossed 100 million units sold. Over the summer, fans were questioning how well Borderlands 4 had done not just in terms of launch sales, but continuing player base, and how that might have affected Gearbox's plans, as they waited for confirmation of a second year of support.

Since launching in September, Borderlands 4 has suffered various controversies, mostly to do with severe PC performance issues. Outspoken CEO Randy Pitchford went on the offensive , responding directly to complaints on social media to Claptrap back at disgruntled fans .

Strauss Zelnick, boss of Gearbox parent company Take-Two, previously admitted that Borderlands 4 sales had suffered “a little bit of softness” as a result of the technical issues, but expressed confidence “it’ll all be made up” given enough time. The Nintendo Switch 2 version was scrapped , with Take-Two saying Gearbox had prioritized continued "improvements" to the game on its existing platforms.

All the while, Borderlands 4 remains on a ‘mixed’ user review rating on Steam. After launching to over 300,000 concurrent players on Valve’s platform, Borderlands 4 now averages a concurrent peak in the four digits. Steam numbers do not paint the entire picture of a game’s popularity as it’s also on consoles, but it’s clear Borderlands 4 could do with a shot in the arm.

articles.title: Appraisal Guide - Probably Stolen Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Appraisals are a good way to make money in Probably Stolen without having to already have something for a customer, or to prepare for a specific market spike.
articles.body:
Appraisals are a good way to make money in Probably Stolen without having to already have something for a customer, or to prepare for a specific market spike. Instead, customers bring their items to you for assessment, and you let them know how much it's worth. You get a small cut of that total price, but only based on whether you do it correctly or not. It can be tricky to get a perfect Appraisal. In this guide, we're going to cover the basics of appraisals to make it easier for you to complete this income method while playing Probably Stolen.

There are a handful of items that you may need to appraise while playing Probably Stolen. The common items include cigarettes and Cybernetic Hands. Before you buy a box of Hemingway Cigarettes from customers, you'll need to ensure the Lettering, Logo, Color, and Security seal. If the Lettering is wrong, the Logo is off, the Font is different, or the Seal is broken (or not even there), you can confront the customers about it to lower the price.

Additionally, you can join the Appraisal Board in Probably Stolen a few days after you open your shop. A representative will appear, asking you to pay the upfront cost. If you accept, you'll be able to place a certificate in your Display Window, offering your services to anyone who brings an item that you can inspect. The first items you get are Cybernetic Hands.

Regardless of what kind of Cybernetic Hand you get, you want to start on the first page. All Cybernetic Hands begin at the base value of 100 . From there, you want to determine the type of material. This builds onto the base value, unless it's Aluminum; then there's nothing to add, and you go to the next page.

You'll then assess the Cybernetic Hand's wear and tear . If it has moderate wear on it, it drops down by a small amount, but if there's significant damage, then it drops the value much more. If it's in perfect condition with no wear or damage, then you keep it at the base value.

The next thing is to determine what type of control interface it has . If you can't tell, or there's no way to identify whether there's any form of control interface, this drops the value, but if there is, the basic voltage adds no value, with an EMG+ or a Neural Interface providing the most value.

The next thing you need to assess is if the model is armored or has a blade . It should look bulkier around the knuckles and back of the fist, as it has an added layer of plating. If it does, add 50 to it, and if it has a blade, add 80. If the model has both armor and a blade, you add both values, which comes out to 130.

The final part you need to assess is if there's a set bonus. A set bonus only applies for a Cybernetic Hand if all requirements are met. If so, then you'll add the set bonus to the final value.

Based on the images we posted for these examples, we'll use them as a good way to break down the price for the Cybernetic Hand. For our example, the material of the hand is Carbon Composite, so we'll add 50. After that, there's no wear or damage to it. We won't take any value away from it. On the base of the model, it has a lightning bolt with a plus, indicating it's an EMG+, so we'll add 45 to our total (we're at 195 right now). After that, it has armor and blade, giving it an extra 50 and 80, for a total of 130. Right now, our value is at 325.

Finally, the last thing is to check the set bonus. This Cybernetic Hand would fall under the Tactical set: it's a Carbon Composite, has an EMG+ neural interface, no wear or damage, and is armored and bladed. We'll add 100 to the final value, coming out to 425. After you give this final amount below your Appraisal Service window, send it back to the customer. They'll provide a small dialogue to indicate the job that you did, and have you do more (if there are others) or depart. If you do a poor job, there's a chance that they could leave, even if they have more items for you to look over.

As you get better at the work, the Appraisal Board shows up again to offer you a promotion. This also comes with an upfront fee, but you get better jobs and get to do additional items (which also come with a manual for you to learn). The money is better, but there's a danger of doing a bad job, and a chance for your certificate to be taken away if it goes poorly enough.

Always refer back to the Appraisal Guide whenever you're examining a client's item that they want you to review. You also want to find a process that works best for you. I recommend going from start to finish with an item before submitting. Additionally, there's no time limit for you to complete these appraisals, so you can take as long as you want before sending it back to a customer.

articles.title: The Avatar: Seven Havens Season 1 Blu-ray and Steelbook Is Up for Preorder at Amazon
articles.body:
The first season of Avatar: Seven Havens has officially wrapped up . Unsurprisingly, it quickly became one of the most popular shows on Paramount+, which has now decided to honor the ATLA tradition of physical media releases.

The first official Blu-ray set for Avatar Seven Havens is now available to preorder for $39.99 at Amazon. A steelbook will also be available for $48.99 , but Amazon hasn't revealed any imagery of the more expensive edition. Amazon also hasn't confirmed a release date for either listing.

articles.title: Zach Cregger Says He Still Wants to 'Have a Hand' in Future Resident Evil Sequels
articles.summary: Resident Evil director Zach Cregger says that he’d still want to “have a hand” in potential sequels for his hit horror adaptation, despite swearing off future “franchise” films.
articles.body:
Resident Evil director Zach Cregger says that he’d still want to "have a hand" in potential sequels for his hit horror adaptation, despite swearing off future "franchise" films.

Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil adaptation was a hit at the box office , but its reception was starkly different among hardcore fans of the original games. Rather than attempting to retell stories players have already experienced, he opted for a different approach by following an average Joe as he navigates the chaos of the Raccoon City Incident — and this rubbed a vocal portion of the fanbase the wrong way.

As a result, Cregger has adamantly decided against ever working on a "franchise" again , a word he used on an episode of The Town with Matthew Belloni .

"If there were five Resident Evil movies that you just produced but didn’t write or direct, would you be okay with that, or not?" the host asked him.

"I would want to have some hand in them," Cregger answered. "I can’t help but have an idea for where that franchise — I’m calling it a franchise — could go. So, certainly."

This isn’t the first time Cregger has mentioned his vision for a sequel to his Resident Evil movie; he spoke about the possibility with The Playlist in September, saying he "can’t help thinking about other places this story could go."

"With Barbarian, I’ve never entertained the idea of a sequel or another movie in that universe because that story is, at its heart, so foul," he continued. "What makes Barbarian interesting is the unfolding of the narrative, not the subject matter. I don’t think I want to write another story about what that movie is about. But this is different. I want to talk about the ending of this movie so badly, because there is a big aspect of it that’s worth discussing. This is a different situation."

As previously mentioned, however, the idea of remaining with the Resident Evil franchise — at least as far as films are concerned — has put a sour taste in his mouth due to fans' reactions to his take on Capcom's flagship horror franchise.

In this same interview, Cregger bemoaned the discourse that surrounded the movie, saying that fans weren’t actually focused on the film itself but instead how well it matched up with the games .

"I think I was frustrated at the conversation around Resident Evil and how much of the conversation really didn't have anything to do with the movie," he said. “It had everything to do with whether the movie was living up to the different standards that different fans of the games had. Whether it was using the characters or not, or what did I get wrong in the lore? It was just a lot about, 'Why isn't this like the source material, or why is it good that it's not like the source material?' All the conversation just felt like it was about not the movie."

Speaking with IGN , Cregger admitted he was "naive" to think that fans would be gung-ho about his take on the source material; though, despite it all, it seems like he’d still want to be attached to future adaptations of Resident Evil in some shape or form.

articles.title: A Buggy World of Warcraft Mount Has Renewed Player Frustrations at the State of Retail
articles.summary: While World of Warcraft Forever is heading to what is likely a monumental release on November 4, some retail World of Warcraft players have been feeling neglected, and a recent mount has become a flashpoint for that frustration.
articles.body:
While World of Warcraft Forever is heading to what is likely a monumental release on November 4, some retail World of Warcraft players have been angry at the state of the game, and a recent mount has become a flashpoint for that frustration.

Blizzard released the 'Hot Motocross Bunmover 4000' mount as part of its November Trading Post, and it's just a cute little tricycle with an oven attached to the back to tie in with Thanksgiving. The problem, though, is that its wheels aren't animated. They also clip through the ground, making it look like it's just sliding around on the floor. In the grand scheme of things, this would have been a minor blip, but the mount has ignited player frustrations that have been simmering for the last year since Midnight released.

Back when Midnight launched, everything seemed great, and it reviewed well. Here at IGN, we gave it a 9, with reviewer Len Hafer saying, "Enthralling zones and a satisfying endgame loop carry World of Warcraft: Midnight from high point to high point." But just like any MMO, the real test is the updates that follow release.

World of Warcraft: Midnight Cinematic Images and First Screenshots

Those updates have been marked by rapid-fire content with 'invasions' that feel like they've been copied and pasted from previous seasons and lackluster writing, culminating in the current patch, which kills off a beloved Horde character pretty much out of the blue. So, when Blizzard released the Hot Motocross Bunmover 4000, it took all of that frustration and gave it a confectionary symbol.

Reddit user iamShorteh posted a screenshot of the mount on Reddit , captioned, "Attached: image of the mount, this is how the wheels remain permanently on the Hot Motocross Bunmover 4000. Literally unplayable." Then, user audioshaman replied, "But Holly Langdale assured me that the 8 week patch cadence has had zero impact on quality." That was followed by user gladfanatic saying, "They straight up don’t care anymore in retail lol."

That eight-week patch cadence started back in Dragonflight as a way to eliminate the long content droughts that the MMO had in past expansions. While it was fine for a while, that schedule has grown problematic over the last couple of expansions, with bugs and repeated content plaguing nearly every patch. It's little wonder, then, why WoW Forever developers told me last week that the Classic+ mode would be opting for a slower update schedule .

But there are some WoW fans that think the problems run deeper than WoW's update schedule. User Jocic posted, "Genuinely, what is happening? At this point, you can't even use the eight-week cadence as an excuse for them. How is EVERYTHING broken?" Even on Twitter, Windows Central Executive Editor Jez Corden retweeted a video of the mount , saying, "Blizz has really phoned it in with World of Warcraft: Retail."

However, while people are frustrated with the state of retail, World of Warcraft has been through harder times. The game has survived the lows of Warlords of Draenor and Shadowlands, even when Classic launched right before the latter. Retail WoW will probably live on through these current quality issues, but hopefully the backlash will at least get Blizzard to at least consider changing up the speed at which it's pumping out new content. It's time to pull the ripcord.

At least in the interim, WoW Forever is on the eve of its full release. Despite the problems with its name reservation system last week, it's shaping up to be a massive game. Even in the beta, WoW Forever devs were shocked at how many people were playing , and once the floodgates open on Wednesday, those numbers are only going to go up.

articles.title: Sony Wants to Buy Your PS5 Console for $400
articles.summary: Sony is offering $400 to people who are willing to part ways with their PS5 and two controllers.
articles.body:
Sony is offering $400 to people who are willing to part ways with their PS5 and two controllers.

As spotted by ResetEra user Jay_Horror , PlayStation is sending out notifications to fans who have the PlayStation app on their phones. The notification tells users that they can trade in their console to Sony and have money sent directly to their bank account. This offer is valued up to $400 for anyone who has a standard PS5 and two controllers. Although trade-in programs, particularly around the holiday season, aren't uncommon for retailers like GameStop, it isn't as normal to see platform holders reaching out directly to customers like this.

It may suggest that Sony is preparing for a shortage of hardware or is interested in pre-owned stock that it can sell at a more affordable price than a brand-new unit. PlayStation 5 consoles are currently $600 - $650, depending on whether you get a disc drive. If you want the more premium PS5 Pro console, it will set you back $900. However, due to the demand for the Pro in the lead-up to GTA 6's release, it has been hard to get one at retail price. As a result, resellers and even retailers like GameStop are selling used PS5 Pros for as much as $1,400 .

If you're someone who bought a PS5 before prices began to jump and don't use it, this isn't a terrible deal. Given the console initially cost $500, getting $400 back (so long as you also acquired an additional controller at some point) is a solid trade-in value. At this point in the PS4's life cycle, you wouldn't have gotten anywhere near close to $400 back at a retailer like GameStop.

articles.title: ‘Those Are the Wrong Reasons to Make a Movie’ — Godzilla Minus Zero Director Takashi Yamazaki on Setting Aside the Urge to One-Up Godzilla Minus One
articles.summary: Godzilla Minus Zero writer, director, and VFX supervisor Takashi Yamazaki says that getting caught up in besting Godzilla Minus One "risked diluting what makes the movie great in the first place."
articles.body:
How does a filmmaker attempt to follow up a history-making movie with an even bigger and better sequel? For Godzilla Minus One and Zero writer, director, and VFX supervisor Takashi Yamazaki, that line of thinking doesn’t even belong in the equation.

“In the beginning I thought, ‘Well, how do I outdo its predecessor and how do we make a movie that's going to win all these awards and it's going to be bigger in scale?’” Yamazaki told IGN during an interview near Godzilla Minus Zero’s debut at the New York Film Festival. “But I think it's very dangerous to create a movie with that type of mindset because you're going to risk diluting what makes the movie great in the first place. So those are the wrong reasons to make a movie and it ends up becoming an antagonist in your moviemaking process.”

Godzilla Minus One was released in 2023 and quickly caught fire. Yamazaki’s take on a post-WWII Godzilla was especially praised for its human-focused story and highly impressive VFX, done with a famously lean team of 35 artists . It went on to beat Hideaki Anno’s 2016 Shin Godzilla at the box office, becoming the highest-grossing Godzilla movie to date . At the 2024 Oscars, where the cast and crew walked the red carpet holding Godzilla figurines and wearing very cool Godzilla shoes, the film took home the trophy for Best Visual Effects.

The win was historic on many levels: It was the first Japanese film to claim the award, minted the first Gen Z winner in the category , and did so with the smallest budget of any other category in more than a decade . (Reports had put the cost between $10–15 million.)

“Godzilla Minus One was loved and so well received by so many around the world and received a lot of awards, which I think was unthinkable when we first set out and went to make it,” Yamazaki said. “So thinking about a sequel, of course, there's gonna be a certain amount of pressure.”

Godzilla Minus Zero is due out in the U.S. this week — it opened in Japan on November 3 for Godzilla Day — and the anticipation is high following its film festival premieres this fall that have been universally rapturous. Naturally, it’s a bigger film in just about every way. First and foremost, it’s got an extra kaiju (which means, a new pair of shoes to go with it). It’s both the first R-rated Godzilla movie and the first Japanese film to be specifically shot for IMAX screens.

At a panel at New York Comic-Con, the aforementioned Gen Z Oscar winner, VFX artist and compositor Tatsuji Nojima, gave an example of just how much more intensive the effects process becomes with that extra screen space: The shot of Godzilla leaping out of the ocean behind a seaplane from the first trailer was made entirely using VFX that required rendering 2 billion particles, versus the 200 million particles needed for an ocean sequence in Godzilla Minus One. (Nojima also shared that the scene was made by just two people: himself and an animator.) Though the exact figures are unknown, Yamazaki has confirmed that the budget was certainly bigger this time around. It’s projected to rake in $25–35 million its opening weekend, according to Box Office Pro , which would more than double Godzilla Minus One’s first weekend earnings of $11.4 million.

Still, for Yamazaki, the important part of making a successful sequel was in rejecting the anxiety of feeling like he needed to one-up Godzilla Minus One at all.

“I think when I decided not to think about it was a huge sense of relief for me and just simply focus on making a movie entertaining, making something fun, making something that has a message,” he said. “The moment where I felt like, yes, I did it was probably when I shed off all that extra pressure and thought, ‘You know what? I'm just going to make a fun movie.’ [That] was my own tipping point.”

Godzilla Minus Zero opens in the U.S. on Friday, November 6. We said it “ups the ante on the carnage, providing plenty of satisfying and visually amazing scenes of giant-monster destruction” in our review .

articles.title: Blackpink's Jisoo Confirms She Referenced Resident Evil's Ada Wong in New Music Video
articles.summary: Blackpink’s Jisoo has confirmed that she referenced Resident Evil’s Ada Wong in the music video for her solo song Addicted.
articles.body:
Blackpink’s Jisoo has confirmed that she referenced Resident Evil’s Ada Wong in the music video for her solo song, Addicted.

The song debuted over Halloween weekend, with its accompanying music video showing Jisoo wearing a variety of different looks. One of these outfits, however, struck a chord with certain members of her fanbase due to how startlingly similar it looked to a character from Resident Evil .

At the beginning of the music video, Jisoo wears a black bob and a red bodycon-style dress — a look that’s basically synonymous with Ada Wong, who almost always wears some variation of this style in each game she appears in.

Fans couldn’t help but notice the similarities and asked the K-pop star if this was intentional on her very own app. “Red outfit + short hair look is totally Ada Wong from Resident Evil,” one wrote.

Surprisingly, Jisoo confirmed that this was actually intentional. "I love Biohazard (Resident Evil) sooo much, so I wanted to copy it,” she said in a reply.

Jisoo is open about her love for Resident Evil; she spoke about the series on Hot Ones earlier this year, saying she was “addicted” to the games.

“It’s fast-paced,” she explained. “Something will suddenly pop out at you, so you have to be quick and process it all and take care of the situation. That’s why it’s able to hold my attention, and time just flies right by.”

Funnily enough, Jisoo isn’t the only K-pop star to draw comparisons with Ada Wong recently; in August, Babymonster’s Asa received similar comments from fans after she posted photos of herself on social media wearing a black bob and a red dress , sparking a cute portmanteau of ‘Asa Wong’ from her fanbase.

While Asa hasn’t yet responded to these remarks, Jisoo is an unabashed fan of the games, to the point where she made sure Ada was somehow represented in her latest song.

In other Resident Evil news, Zach Cregger, who directed the series’ most recent movie adaptation, said he would still like to be involved in some way if a sequel gets made, though not as a director. Thus far, it’s unclear whether or not another Resi movie is in the works, but given that Capcom has doubled down on its plans to continue expanding its IP with merch, new content, and movies, it’s possible that we get another look at Raccoon City — especially given how successful the first film was at the box office .

articles.title: Terminally Ill GTA 6 Fan Dies 3 Weeks Before Game's Launch, Fans Pay Their Respects
articles.summary: A terminally ill GTA 6 fan has died three weeks before the game's launch.
articles.body:
A terminally ill GTA 6 fan has died three weeks before the game's launch.

Back in August, a man named Jerry, known online as Void Only, made a viral TikTok video revealing that he had been hospitalized due to an interstitial lung disease and was in need of a lung transplant. However, he noted that his unique situation meant that his lungs were attached to his chest wall, and any surgery would be bloody and dangerous. In that same post, he noted that he just wanted to play GTA 6, and poked fun at Rockstar's many delays for the game. In the comments, fellow players rallied around him and were rooting for him to keep going until the release of GTA 6.

A GoFundMe was set up to pay for his transplant and other needs, with supporters donating $50,000 in a matter of days . In September, Jerry got his transplant, but various complications eventually caused him to lose function of his body. Jerry's sister confirmed via his socials that he died over the weekend, but was extremely appreciative of all of the people who tried to help and support him. The news comes just three weeks before GTA 6's release, which Jerry had planned to stream with his community once it was released.

In the comments of his sister's post, fans expressed sadness over Jerry not being able to make it to the release of the game he'd been excitedly waiting so long to play.

"I was really rooting for him. I'm sorry for your loss," said one commenter.

"I'm adding Void to my gamertag in his honor when GTA releases," said another.

This tragic outcome has left supporters devastated. Jerry himself stayed optimistic in his final months and kept a positive attitude, prompting fans to echo his enthusiasm. Jerry's sister also noted that his mother is planning to do a balloon release in his honor, and more details will be shared at a later date.
